questions.question: How does insurance helps in loss prevention?
questions.solution_html:
• Insurance motivates policyholders to adopt risk-reducing measures (e.g., fire alarms, health
  • checkups) since better safety records can reduce premiums through mechanisms like the No Claim
  • Bonus. ((1.5 Marks)). Insurers conduct risk surveys and issue safety guidelines to policyholders, acting
  • as a preventive mechanism beyond mere compensation. ((1.5 Marks))
questions.final_answer: as a preventive mechanism beyond mere compensation. ()

questions.question: Write a note on evolution of IRDAI.
questions.solution_html:
• IRDAI was established under the IRDA Act, 1999, based on the Malhotra Committee
  • recommendations (1993) which called for an independent regulatory body. ((1 Mark)). It replaced the
  • Controller of Insurance and opened the sector to private and foreign companies (as JVs), ending LIC's
  • monopoly. ((1 Mark)). Headquartered in Hyderabad, IRDAI regulates and develops the insurance
  • industry while protecting policyholders' interests. ((1 Mark))

questions.question: Why is “trust” considered the ultimate product in insurance.
questions.solution_html:
• Insurance is a promise, not a physical product. The customer pays today for future compensation
  • they may never need — trust is what makes that promise credible. ((1.5 Marks)). Without confidence in
  • the insurer's reliability, claim settlement record, and financial strength, no customer will buy a policy.
  • Trust is therefore the core of the insurance relationship. ((1.5 Marks))
questions.final_answer: Trust is therefore the core of the insurance relationship. ()
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain secondary social groups.
questions.solution_html:
• Secondary social groups are larger, more impersonal groups where relationships are formal
  • indirect, and goal-oriented (e.g., trade unions, professional associations, employer organizations). (1.5
  • Marks). In insurance, secondary groups influence buying behaviour through shared experiences, word
  • of-mouth recommendations, and group insurance schemes offered via employers or professional
  • bodies. ((1.5 Marks))

questions.question: What role do family values play in insurance purchasing?
questions.solution_html:
• Values like financial security for dependents, responsibility, and long-term planning strongly drive
  • life and health insurance purchases. ((1.5 Marks)). Joint families may prefer group or family floater
  • plans, while nuclear families prioritize individual term and health policies tailored to specific financial
  • goals. ((1.5 Marks))

questions.question: Define the individual agency system of insurance marketing.
questions.solution_html:
• The individual agency system involves licensed agents who exclusively represent a single
  • insurance company and sell its products on its behalf, acting as appointed intermediaries. ((1.5 Marks)).
  • Agents earn commissions on premiums collected and are responsible for prospecting, advising clients
  • and post-sale servicing. It is the most traditional and widespread distribution channel in India. (1.5
  • Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is underwriting?
questions.solution_html:
• Underwriting is the process by which an insurance company evaluates an applicant's risk profile
  • to decide whether to accept the proposal and at what premium rate. ((1.5 Marks)). It involves assessing
  • factors like age, health status, occupation, habits, and lifestyle to classify the applicant as a standard
  • substandard, or preferred risk. ((1.5 Marks))

questions.question: What are online aggregators?
questions.solution_html:
• Online aggregators are digital platforms (e.g., Policybazaar, Coverfox) that allow consumers to
  • compare insurance products from multiple companies based on premium, features, and coverage in
  • one place. ((1.5 Marks)). They simplify the buying process, promote price transparency, and empower
  • customers to make informed choices without visiting individual insurers. ((1.5 Marks))

questions.question: What is meant by sales promotion in insurance?
questions.solution_html:
• Sales promotion refers to short-term incentives designed to stimulate the purchase or renewal of
  • insurance policies, such as premium discounts, bonus covers, free riders, or loyalty rewards. (1.5
  • Marks). Referral bonuses for agents, premium waiver offers, NCB (No Claim Bonus) discounts, and
  • targeted campaigns for women, senior citizens, or rural segments. ((1.5 Marks))
questions.final_answer: targeted campaigns for women, senior citizens, or rural segments. ()

questions.question: What is post-sale service in insurance?
questions.solution_html:
• Post-sale service refers to all activities by the insurer after the policy is issued, aimed at maintaining
  • customer satisfaction, trust, and long-term retention. ((1.5 Marks)). Policy servicing (address/nominee
  • changes), renewal reminders, claim assistance, grievance redressal, and periodic policy reviews to
  • match the customer's evolving needs. ((1.5 Marks))

questions.question: What is meant by digital marketing in insurance?
questions.solution_html:
• Digital marketing in insurance refers to the use of online channels — social media, email, search
  • engines, websites, and apps — to promote insurance products and acquire customers. ((1.5 Marks)). It
  • enables targeted, data-driven campaigns, reduces customer acquisition cost, allows real-time
  • engagement, and helps reach tech-savvy younger demographics. ((1.5 Marks))
questions.final_answer: engagement, and helps reach tech-savvy younger demographics. ()

questions.question: Examine how IRDAI contributes to the growth and development of insurance industry
questions.solution_html:
• IRDAI frames and enforces regulations on licensing, solvency margins, product approvals, and
  • agent conduct — ensuring the financial soundness of insurers and protecting policyholders from
  • malpractice ((2 Marks)). By opening the market to private and foreign players (as JVs post-1999)
  • IRDAI fostered competition, product innovation (ULIPs, micro-insurance, health insurance), and
  • improved overall service quality ((2 Marks)). IRDAI mandates grievance redressal mechanisms
  • regulates claim settlement timelines, and runs public awareness campaigns — building trust and
  • confidence in the insurance sector ((2 Marks)).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: The insurance marketing mix "focuses on building trust, clarity and accessibility." Explain how the elements of "Product" and "Price" specifically contribute to achieving this focus.
questions.solution_html:
• In insurance, the product is an intangible policy — a promise of future compensation. Trust and
  • clarity are built through transparently worded policy documents with clear benefits, exclusions, and
  • claim procedures. Relevant riders and add-on cover that address specific needs make the product more
  • meaningful and accessible to diverse customer segments ((3 Marks)). Pricing must be perceived as
  • equitable to build trust. Competitive and fair premiums, flexible payment modes (monthly, quarterly
  • annual), and discount mechanisms like NCB (No Claim Bonus) make insurance financially accessible.
  • Transparent premium calculation — explaining how age, health, and coverage affect cost — reassures
  • customers and reinforces confidence in the insurer ((3 Marks)).
questions.final_answer: customers and reinforces confidence in the insurer ()
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the scope of market research.
questions.solution_html:
• Any 4 of the following ((1.5 marks) each)
  •  Consumer Research: Studying policyholder behaviour, needs, preferences, and satisfaction
  • levels to design better products and target communication effectively.
  •  Product Research: Identifying gaps in existing insurance offerings and developing new
  • products for emerging risks (e.g., cyber insurance, parametric insurance).
  •  Market Analysis: Assessing market size, growth trends, competitive landscape, and the impact
  • of regulatory changes to inform strategic planning.
  •  Distribution Research: Evaluating the performance of different channels (agents
  • bancassurance, online aggregators, direct sales) to optimize reach and reduce costs.
  •  Advertising Research: Measuring the effectiveness of promotional campaigns and identifying
  • the most impactful communication strategies for target segments.
questions.final_answer: the most impactful communication strategies for target segments
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe ULIPs and their features.
questions.solution_html:
• A ULIP (Unit Linked Insurance Plan) is a hybrid financial product that combines life insurance
  • protection with market-linked investment, regulated by IRDAI with a mandatory 5-year lock-in period
  • (Definition :(2 Marks))
  • Key Features ((1 mark) each, any 4)
  •  Dual Benefit: Provides both a death benefit (life cover) and returns from market-linked
  • fund performance.
  •  Fund Choice: Policyholders choose from equity, debt, or balanced funds based on their risk
  • appetite, and can switch between funds.
  •  Transparency: NAV (Net Asset Value) is declared daily; all charges (mortality, admin, fund
  • management) are disclosed upfront.
  •  Flexibility: Allows partial withdrawals, top-up premiums, and fund switching after the 5
  • year lock-in period.
  •  Tax Benefits: Premiums qualify for deduction under Section 80C; maturity proceeds are
  • exempt under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act.
questions.final_answer: exempt under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain underwriting guidelines and their importance in insurance operations.
questions.solution_html:
• Underwriting guidelines are a standardized set of rules and criteria established by an insurance
  • company to ensure consistency, fairness, and discipline in risk assessment and policy acceptance
  • decisions across all applicants (Definition :(2 Marks)).
  • Key Guidelines Include
  •  Age and health limits for acceptance of proposals.
  •  Premium loading (extra charge) for substandard or high-risk individuals.
  •  Mandatory medical examinations above specified sum assured thresholds.
  •  Exclusions for pre-existing medical conditions.
  • Importance ((4 Marks))
  •  Consistency: Ensures all applicants are evaluated on uniform parameters, preventing bias or
  • arbitrary decisions.
  •  Prevents Adverse Selection: Stops only high-risk individuals from purchasing coverage
  • protecting the insurer's risk pool.
  •  Financial Solvency: Avoids excessive risk concentration that could threaten the insurer's ability
  • to pay claims.
  •  Policyholder Protection: Sustainable underwriting keeps premiums viable and ensures long
  • term claim-paying capacity.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain how technology helps insurance advertising and promotion.
questions.solution_html:
• Digital Advertising ((2 Marks)): Social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube) and search
  • engines enable targeted ads based on demographics, browsing behaviour, and interests allowing
  • insurers to reach the right customer at the right time with cost efficiency.
  • AI and Data Analytics ((2 Marks)): AI-powered tools analyse customer data to personalize
  • promotional messages, predict purchase intent, and optimize campaign performance
  • significantly improving conversion rates.
  • Chatbots and Automation ((1 Mark)): Chatbots provide 24/7 engagement during promotional
  • campaigns, instantly answering customer queries and guiding prospects through the purchase
  • journey without human intervention.
  • Content and Video Marketing ((1 Mark)): Explainer videos, infographics, blogs, and webinars
  • simplify complex insurance concepts, educate potential buyers, and build long-term brand trust
  • online.

questions.question: Explain the evolution of insurance industry in India.
questions.solution_html:
• Pre-Independence Era ((2 Marks)): Life insurance began in 1818 with the Oriental Life Insurance
  • Company, primarily serving Europeans. Indian lives were charged higher premiums. The Bombay
  • Mutual Life Assurance Society (1870) was the first Indian-owned company to insure Indian lives at
  • standard rates. The Insurance Act of 1938 introduced basic regulatory oversight.
  • Post-Independence & Nationalization ((2 Marks)): LIC was established in 1956 by nationalizing
  • all private life insurers, creating a state monopoly focused on spreading insurance awareness
  • to rural India and channelling savings into national development. General Insurance
  • Corporation (GIC) was formed in 1972 for non-life insurance.
  • Liberalization & Modern Era ((2 Marks)): The Malhotra Committee (1993) recommended
  • sweeping reforms; IRDAI was established in 1999, ending state monopolies and allowing
  • private and foreign players (as joint ventures). This triggered product innovation, improved
  • service quality, and rapid premium growth. Digital channels and InsurTech (AI, big data
  • mobile apps) have further transformed the industry in the 21st century.
questions.final_answer: mobile apps) have further transformed the industry in the 21st century
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

  • malpractice ((2 Marks)). By opening the market to private and foreign players (as JVs post-1999)
  • IRDAI fostered competition, product innovation (ULIPs, micro-insurance, health insurance), and
  • improved overall service quality ((2 Marks)). IRDAI mandates grievance redressal mechanisms
  • regulates claim settlement timelines, and runs public awareness campaigns — building trust and
  • confidence in the insurance sector ((2 Marks)).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: The insurance marketing mix "focuses on building trust, clarity and accessibility." Explain how the elements of "Product" and "Price" specifically contribute to achieving this focus.
questions.solution_html:
• In insurance, the product is an intangible policy — a promise of future compensation. Trust and
  • clarity are built through transparently worded policy documents with clear benefits, exclusions, and
  • claim procedures. Relevant riders and add-on cover that address specific needs make the product more
  • meaningful and accessible to diverse customer segments ((3 Marks)). Pricing must be perceived as
  • equitable to build trust. Competitive and fair premiums, flexible payment modes (monthly, quarterly
  • annual), and discount mechanisms like NCB (No Claim Bonus) make insurance financially accessible.
  • Transparent premium calculation — explaining how age, health, and coverage affect cost — reassures
  • customers and reinforces confidence in the insurer ((3 Marks)).
questions.final_answer: customers and reinforces confidence in the insurer ()

questions.question: Discuss the scope of market research.
questions.solution_html:
• Any 4 of the following ((1.5 marks) each)
  •  Consumer Research: Studying policyholder behaviour, needs, preferences, and satisfaction
  • levels to design better products and target communication effectively.
  •  Product Research: Identifying gaps in existing insurance offerings and developing new
  • products for emerging risks (e.g., cyber insurance, parametric insurance).
  •  Market Analysis: Assessing market size, growth trends, competitive landscape, and the impact
  • of regulatory changes to inform strategic planning.
  •  Distribution Research: Evaluating the performance of different channels (agents
  • bancassurance, online aggregators, direct sales) to optimize reach and reduce costs.
  •  Advertising Research: Measuring the effectiveness of promotional campaigns and identifying
  • the most impactful communication strategies for target segments.
questions.final_answer: the most impactful communication strategies for target segments

questions.question: Describe ULIPs and their features.
questions.solution_html:
• A ULIP (Unit Linked Insurance Plan) is a hybrid financial product that combines life insurance
  • protection with market-linked investment, regulated by IRDAI with a mandatory 5-year lock-in period
  • (Definition :(2 Marks))
  • Key Features ((1 mark) each, any 4)
  •  Dual Benefit: Provides both a death benefit (life cover) and returns from market-linked
  • fund performance.
  •  Fund Choice: Policyholders choose from equity, debt, or balanced funds based on their risk
  • appetite, and can switch between funds.
  •  Transparency: NAV (Net Asset Value) is declared daily; all charges (mortality, admin, fund
  • management) are disclosed upfront.
  •  Flexibility: Allows partial withdrawals, top-up premiums, and fund switching after the 5
  • year lock-in period.
  •  Tax Benefits: Premiums qualify for deduction under Section 80C; maturity proceeds are
  • exempt under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act.
questions.final_answer: exempt under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain underwriting guidelines and their importance in insurance operations.
questions.solution_html:
• Underwriting guidelines are a standardized set of rules and criteria established by an insurance
  • company to ensure consistency, fairness, and discipline in risk assessment and policy acceptance
  • decisions across all applicants (Definition :(2 Marks)).
  • Key Guidelines Include
  •  Age and health limits for acceptance of proposals.
  •  Premium loading (extra charge) for substandard or high-risk individuals.
  •  Mandatory medical examinations above specified sum assured thresholds.
  •  Exclusions for pre-existing medical conditions.
  • Importance ((4 Marks))
  •  Consistency: Ensures all applicants are evaluated on uniform parameters, preventing bias or
  • arbitrary decisions.
  •  Prevents Adverse Selection: Stops only high-risk individuals from purchasing coverage
  • protecting the insurer's risk pool.
  •  Financial Solvency: Avoids excessive risk concentration that could threaten the insurer's ability
  • to pay claims.
  •  Policyholder Protection: Sustainable underwriting keeps premiums viable and ensures long
  • term claim-paying capacity.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain how technology helps insurance advertising and promotion.
questions.solution_html:
• Digital Advertising ((2 Marks)): Social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube) and search
  • engines enable targeted ads based on demographics, browsing behaviour, and interests allowing
  • insurers to reach the right customer at the right time with cost efficiency.
  • AI and Data Analytics ((2 Marks)): AI-powered tools analyse customer data to personalize
  • promotional messages, predict purchase intent, and optimize campaign performance

  • Chatbots and Automation ((1 Mark)): Chatbots provide 24/7 engagement during promotional

  • journey without human intervention.
  • Content and Video Marketing ((1 Mark)): Explainer videos, infographics, blogs, and webinars
  • simplify complex insurance concepts, educate potential buyers, and build long-term brand trust
  • online.

questions.question: Explain the evolution of insurance industry in India.
questions.solution_html:
• Pre-Independence Era ((2 Marks)): Life insurance began in 1818 with the Oriental Life Insurance
  • Company, primarily serving Europeans. Indian lives were charged higher premiums. The Bombay
  • Mutual Life Assurance Society (1870) was the first Indian-owned company to insure Indian lives at
  • standard rates. The Insurance Act of 1938 introduced basic regulatory oversight.
  • Post-Independence & Nationalization ((2 Marks)): LIC was established in 1956 by nationalizing
  • all private life insurers, creating a state monopoly focused on spreading insurance awareness
  • to rural India and channelling savings into national development. General Insurance
  • Corporation (GIC) was formed in 1972 for non-life insurance.
  • Liberalization & Modern Era ((2 Marks)): The Malhotra Committee (1993) recommended
  • sweeping reforms; IRDAI was established in 1999, ending state monopolies and allowing
  • private and foreign players (as joint ventures). This triggered product innovation, improved
  • service quality, and rapid premium growth. Digital channels and InsurTech (AI, big data
  • mobile apps) have further transformed the industry in the 21st century.
questions.final_answer: mobile apps) have further transformed the industry in the 21st century
